To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antiCEA antibodies can be purified by absorption with a P-factor.
the P-factor is an antiCEA factor and the antiCEA sera absorbed with the P-factor acquire higher tumor specificity.

(i) the CEA molecule is a glycoprotein, (ii) the CEA antigen is a complex antigen, (iii) the CEA is a family of antigens, (iv) the CEA antigens are present in normal tissues, and (v) the CEA molecules are present in normal cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the P-factor, a plasma component reacting with a number of antiCEA sera.
the identification and characterization of a plasma factor which reacts with antiCEA antibodies and with the isolation of an antiCEA antiserum with high tumor specificity.
the identification of the plasma factor reacting with the antiCEA sera; the P-factor may be a useful reagent for obtaining antiCEA sera more specific for the neoplastic tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, at least, 2 distinct antigens, one present in normal colonic mucosal cells and granulocytes (CEA) and the other present in colonic adenocarci-noma (the P-factor), are recognized by some antisera to CEA.
the P-absorbtion of the antiCEA sera is not the only factor that determines the specificity of the resulting anti-CEA sera.
the P-factor is a normal serum component which is present in the circulation and is not a tumor-associated antigen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CEA molecule is present in normal tissues and in tumor cells, but the P-absorbing factor is present in normal plasma and in tumor tissues.

the P-factor is a plasma component reacting with the anti-CEA sera and that the anti-CEAs sera absorbed with the P-factor are unreactive with colonic granulocytes and normal colonic mucosae, and selectively reactive with colonic adenocarci-nomas.

the anti-CEA antibodies present in the sera of the patients with colorectal cancer react not only with the CEA but also with a plasma factor, the so-called P-factor, that is present in normal human plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to achieve a higher tumor specificity of the antiCEA sera and to reduce the number of false positive reactions, it is necessary to absorb the antiCEA serum with a plasma factor.
antiCEA sera can be improved by P-absorption to acquire higher tumor specificity.
, in order to obtain antiCEAs with higher tumor specificity, it is not sufficient to absorb them only with CEA.
